use_case: AI credit underwriting model: scores consumer installment loan applications (up to $50,000) and small business credit line applications (up to $250,000); returns a score, a recommendation, and the top 4 reason codes to loan origination
business_owner: Bank consumer and small business lending executive
vendor_or_model: In-house gradient-boosted model served on provider A (SYS-B3); uses cash-flow attributes from the Financial Software data service (AI-005)
data_categories: Credit bureau attributes; application data; deposit account cash-flow attributes; for small business, business credit data and owners' personal credit scores (customer information and NPI)
human_in_the_loop: Consumer: the model auto-decides about 70% of applications inside credit policy cutoffs; the rest go to underwriters. Small business: underwriters decide every application; from 2026-10-15 a second officer reviews every model-recommended decline
applicable_laws: ECOA and Regulation B (12 CFR 1002.4(a), 1002.6(b), 1002.9); GLBA and 12 CFR 30 App. B; group model risk policy (independent validation); Colorado SB26-189 not applicable today (no Colorado lending footprint)
status: In production with conditions (P10 section 6); small business expansion on hold

use_case: Wire and ACH payment fraud scoring: scores outgoing business payments and holds high-risk ones for review
business_owner: Bank contact center and fraud director
vendor_or_model: In-house model with a vendor device-intelligence feed
data_categories: Payment details, beneficiary history, device and session data (customer information)
consequential_decision_category: None (fraud prevention; held payments are reviewed by staff)
human_in_the_loop: Fraud analysts review every hold and release or return the payment
applicable_laws: GLBA and 12 CFR 30 App. B (III.C.1.f monitoring); group model risk policy
status: In production; monthly challenger model from 2026-11

use_case: AML alert prioritization: ranks transaction monitoring alerts for investigators
vendor_or_model: Monitoring software vendor's machine learning module
data_categories: Transactions and customer risk data (customer information; SAR-related data)
consequential_decision_category: None directly (investigators decide; SAR decisions stay human)
human_in_the_loop: Investigators work every alert above threshold and a sample below it
applicable_laws: 12 CFR 21.11; GLBA and 12 CFR 30 App. B; group model risk policy

use_case: Contact center generative assistant: drafts answers for agents from policy documents and, after caller verification, account data
business_owner: Bank contact center and fraud director
vendor_or_model: Enterprise large language model service with no-training terms
data_categories: Policy documents; account data after verification (customer information)
human_in_the_loop: Agents read, edit, and deliver every answer; the assistant never acts on accounts
applicable_laws: GLBA and 12 CFR 30 App. B; POL-04 4.9; group AI Standard
status: In production for 600 agents; expansion paused until output sampling starts

use_case: Cash-flow data service: attributes and a cash-flow score derived from deposit account transactions, delivered to 64 client banks and to the bank (AI-001)
vendor_or_model: In-house model and attribute library on SYS-S2
data_categories: Client banks' customers' deposit transactions (client customer information held as a service provider)
consequential_decision_category: Credit (client banks use it in credit decisions)
human_in_the_loop: Client banks decide how to use the score; the division does not make credit decisions. Documentation of intended use and human review is not yet provided
applicable_laws: Client contracts and SOC 2 commitments; FTC Act Sec. 5 (N51-R01); client banks' ECOA and Regulation B duties; Bank Service Company Act (12 U.S.C. 1867(c)); Colorado SB26-189 developer duties for 3 Colorado client banks (effective 2027-01-01; under counsel review)
status: In production for 64 client banks; new client sales paused until conditions are met
